families.concept: The dead who were buried whole because there was no fire left to burn them, risen to look for the pyre they were promised.
families.lore: In 瑟蘭 the dead were always given to the fire and their ash carried up to the Sun-Forge. When the Forge died there was no fuel to waste on corpses, so a thousand years of dead went into the ground whole — 未焚者, the Unburnt. They rise carrying what they were buried with (kettle caps, grave-linen, funeral urns, coffin boards) and walk toward any warmth, because warmth is the pyre they are owed. The Hushed Order's bishops conscript them, but they need no master to envy a living fire. Everything they do is stiff soldier-drill or grave goods used as weapons; nothing is magic. Death: they fall apart joint by joint and the bones finally burn — one quick flare of pale ember, then ash: the cremation they were waiting for.
families.roles_lack: caster — bones fight only with what they were buried with; their magic belongs to the Order priests who march with them, so a bone pack is dangerous in proportion to who is leading it.

families.concept: Living people who went too long without ember-light: the warmth left, the hunger stayed.
families.lore: Husks are not the dead. They are villagers, pilgrims and beacon-keepers whose fire went out and who did not die of it — 失燼, ember-loss. The body cools to the temperature of the dusk, the mind narrows to a single want, and what is left follows warmth the way water runs downhill: lamps, cook-fires, the heat in another person's chest. Families chained them up or locked them out rather than kill them, so husks still wear nightshirts, bindings and tether-chains, and many clutch a dead lantern they cannot put down. They attack with hands and teeth and pile onto anything warm. Death: a husk does not crumble at once — the last of its body heat leaves as a breath of orange sparks, and only then does the grey flesh flake to ash.
families.roles_lack: ranged and caster — a husk fight is a pure rush from every side; the Coldcaller makes the rush bigger instead of giving it a back line.

families.concept: The order that calls the dusk a mercy and puts out every fire it finds.
families.lore: The Order teaches that the Sun-Forge did not fail — it was allowed to rest — and that every lamp lit since is a scream in a house of sleep. Its members take the vow of quiet (lips sewn or masked), carry snuffers instead of torches, and travel with wet shrouds, cold censers and bells whose clappers have been cut out. They are living people, organised and drilled: a complete army with skirmishers, line troops, marksmen, priests, healers and champions, which is why they are the one family that has every role. Their weapons extinguish — snuffer-poles, bolts that eat light, smoke that mends their own. Death: silent; the body folds, the mask falls, and the ash is black with a rim of white sparks — their own fire, finally let out.
families.roles_lack: nothing — the Order is the game's reference "full army"; every other family is defined by what it is missing compared with this one.

families.concept: Souls that no pyre released, chained to their own shrouds by the Order as wardens and as proof.
families.lore: A soul was meant to rise with the smoke. With no pyre it stays where the body fell and slowly forgets everything but the cold. The Order finds these and keeps them — a chain twice round the shroud, a seal with the Order's mark — as wardens, and as evidence that rest is kinder than fire. Wraiths are drawn to the ember in the hero the way the Unburnt are, but they cannot hold it: their touch only takes heat. They drift through walls of bodies, blink away from blades, and nest in dead lanterns. Death: the chain drops, the shroud collapses empty, and one small warm spark rises straight up — the only monsters whose ash goes upward.
families.roles_lack: bruiser, ranged physical and every kind of support — wraiths are solitary griefs, each alone even in a pack; they never help each other, so the family has no force multiplier and is always a garnish on someone else's pack.

families.concept: People who stopped tending fire and started stealing it — raiders who sell stolen embers to anyone, the Order included.
families.lore: Keeping a beacon alive costs a village everything it has. The Ember-takers decided long ago that it is easier to take a fire than to feed one: they break small beacons, strip caravans and carry the stolen embers off in iron cages to sell — to frightened towns at a ruinous price, or to the Order, which pays well for fires to put out. They are ordinary living people, and that is the unsettling part. They smear cold ash on their skin so husks cannot feel their warmth, wear strings of dead lanterns as tallies, and fight with a lamplighter's trade tools turned into weapons: hook-poles, wick-shears, oil pots. No magic at all. Death: they die like people — a real fall, no crumble; only when the stolen ember they carried gutters out does the body ash with it.
families.roles_lack: caster and healer — they are thieves, not believers: nothing they own is magic and nobody stops to help anybody.

families.concept: The animals that survived a thousand sunless years by learning to hunt heat.
families.lore: Nothing that needed the sun is left. What remains has spent a thousand years learning one trick: find warmth and take it. Dusk-fauna are pale, large-eared or eyeless, with heat-pits instead of eyes and coats full of ash; they sleep on old hearth-stones and warm brass and follow travellers for the heat of their lamps. They are not evil — they are hungry — and they are the only family that comes to the hero out of appetite rather than belief or grief. Each region has its own beasts. Attacks are bites, charges, swoops and pounces; several steal the hero's resource (the ember) instead of life. Death: an animal death — they drop, kick once, and the ash that takes them is plain grey with no sparks at all.
families.roles_lack: caster, support and reviver — they are animals; nothing in the family thinks about the fight.

families.concept: The garrison of the pass, frozen at its posts and still holding them.
families.lore: 凍骨關 was held by a garrison sworn to keep the pass beacon alight. When the fuel trains stopped they burned the stockade, then their spear-shafts, then sat down around the cold brazier in rank order and froze. Their oath outlasted them. The Frostbound still stand watch, still answer the horn, still walk the supply road behind a dead mule — and the mountain hunters who came to loot them froze too, and became the horned stalkers that run ahead of the line. Ice has grown through them like a second armour and fused their weapons to their hands. Attacks are drilled spear-work, horn-blasts of killing wind and the slow weight of ice. Death: they shatter — the ice goes first in a burst of shards, then the body inside falls to ash that the wind takes sideways.
families.roles_lack: a true caster and a reviver — their only magic is the cold itself, delivered by horn and by weather; ranged pressure comes from the frost-skinned Unburnt javelineers that march with them.

families.concept: The last flames of dead beacons, frozen mid-flicker into blue glass that burns cold.
families.lore: When a beacon dies in the high pass its last flame does not go out. It freezes: a tongue of fire turned to blue glass, still moving, a flicker that takes an hour. The Order holds these up as proof that fire itself wants to rest. They are right that the flames no longer suffer — they are hungry. A frozen flame burns backwards: it draws heat in. They drift down from the dead beacons, cluster on anything warm and take the fire out of it, and the glass-mites that graze on them carry shards of it on their backs. Every attack is cold: shard volleys, heat-draining auras, slow crushing embraces. Death: they crack with a sound like a struck glass, and for one instant the flame inside thaws and burns its true colour — a flash of warm orange — before it goes out.
families.roles_lack: line melee, support and anything fast on foot — an elemental family that is all area and attrition, meant to be mixed with Frostbound infantry who pin the hero inside its zones.

families.scope: home F; also W, S, A
families.concept: The giants who carried fuel to the Sun-Forge, still hauling a thousand years after it went out.
families.lore: The Sun-Forge ate forests. To feed it the old kings bound a people of giants — 薪役, the Fuel-bearers — by an oath sworn on the Forge itself: carry until the fire is fed. The fire was never fed again, so the oath never ended. They walk the old fuel roads from the passes down to the abyss with hods the size of carts, picking up anything that will burn: timber, coal, oil, furniture and — now that there is little else — anything warm. A Fuel-bearer is not cruel; it does not distinguish between a log and a traveller. They appear singly among other families' packs. Attacks are loads swung, thrown and dropped. Death: the giant kneels, sets its load down with care, and only then crumbles; the hod stays behind as a prop.
families.roles_lack: every small role — by design this is the "one giant in someone else's pack" family; it never spawns as a pack of its own and has no swarmers, casters or support.

families.concept: Carrion beetles the undertakers once kept to clean bones — grown huge on a thousand years of unburnt dead, and still burying everything they find.
families.lore: When the pyres stopped, the gravediggers needed helpers: burying-beetles, bred to strip and inter the dead quickly. The trade died; the beetles did not. Grown to the size of dogs and oxen on a thousand years of graves, they do what they were bred for with patient thoroughness: find a body, dig under it, let it sink, cover it. They are not particular about whether the body has stopped moving. They nest in coffins and wear grave goods caught on their shells. Attacks: bites, undermining the ground beneath the hero (rooted — interred to the knees), larvae that pour out of anything dead. Death: they flip onto their backs with the legs folding inward; the ash is black and greasy.
families.roles_lack: ranged, caster and support — pure vermin pressure from below; wastes packs get their reach from the Unburnt.

families.concept: The half-burnt forest of the first winter — trees that were set alight and never finished burning.
families.lore: In the first winter after the Forge died, people burned the forests of the wastes to stay alive. The fires went out before the trees were consumed, and charcoal holds heat for a very long time. The Charwood are those trees: black, split, hollow, with a seam of ember still creeping somewhere inside them after a thousand years. They want what any half-burnt thing wants — to finish. They move toward fire to complete their own burning, and they remember who lit them. Fire damage ignites them: a lit Charwood is faster and deadlier but is burning itself to death. Attacks: branch-clubs, roots from below, a noose of the ropes people were hanged with for hoarding wood. Death: they collapse inward into a heap of glowing charcoal that takes several seconds to go dark.
families.roles_lack: ranged, caster and support — the forest only holds ground; it is slow, and the danger is being rooted in the middle of it. (In the mire it appears as waterlogged bog-wood that cannot be ignited.)

families.concept: Hollow figures of packed ash standing where people burned, walked by the wind that blows up from the abyss.
families.lore: Where many burned at once — the last great pyres, the towns that set themselves alight for one warm night — the ash kept their shapes. 灰塑 are hollow casts: a crust of packed ash around the space where a person was, standing or kneeling exactly as they died. The wind that rises from the abyss walks them. They are fragile and patient; break one and the ash sifts back together unless the pile is scattered. Fire cannot hurt what is already burnt. Attacks: choking embraces, ash blown into eyes and lungs (weaken), the sheer weight of a drift. Death: the game's signature death taken literally — they fall into a pile, and the pile may stand up again.
families.roles_lack: swarmer, ranged physical, support and healer — the standard cast effectively dies twice, which is the family's substitute for numbers; immune to burn.

families.concept: Spiders the barrow-wardens kept to wrap the dead in silk when there was no fire to burn them — still wrapping everything.
families.lore: A wrapped corpse does not rise. The old barrow-wardens knew it and kept 織殮蛛, shroud-spiders, to bind each body in silk before the lid went on. The wardens are gone; the spiders have kept the rite. Every web in the Catacombs is a winding-sheet, the cocoons hang in neat rows like a congregation, and the weavers treat anything that moves as a body not yet properly dressed. Their silk is grey with ash. Some cocoons are neither empty nor dead, and walk on strings. Attacks: binding silk (root), drops from the vault, bites that numb (slow). Death: they curl up with the legs drawn in tight; the silk they carried unravels in the air as threads of ash.
families.roles_lack: caster and a hard-hitting bruiser — the threat is being held still while something else arrives, not being hit hard by the spiders themselves.

families.concept: The carved likenesses on the barrow-lids, woken by the Order's rites of silence in place of the bones beneath them.
families.lore: The barrow-lords lie under stone lids carved in their own likeness, flat on their backs with hands joined. The Order's rite of quiet is meant to still restless bones; said over a sarcophagus it does that — and wakes the stone instead. The effigies sit up and step down still shaped for lying: a slab of lid on their backs, hands that cannot unclasp, feet turned out — and the stone hounds carved at their feet get up with them. In the Sanctum the marble saints of the cathedral have followed them. They are slow, almost impossible to stagger and unimpressed by fire. Attacks: stone weight, blade-edges that were never sharpened, bowing prayers that send a line of crushing quiet across the floor. Death: they crack along old mason's joints and fall into rubble blocks — the one family that leaves stone, not ash; the ash sifts out of the cracks afterwards.
families.roles_lack: swarmer and support — stone is never numerous and never helps its neighbour; an effigy pack is three or four heavy pieces (and perhaps one hound) that must be fought in the order they reach you.

families.concept: The boardwalk-folk who traded fire for the warmth of rot, and were kept by the peat.
families.lore: The marsh people could not keep fires lit on water, but they found another warmth: rot gives off heat. The hags taught them to sleep buried in fermenting peat, and for a generation it worked. Then the sleepers stopped getting up the same. 沼裔 are what the peat gave back — still fishing, still netting, still tending their hearth-toads, with bog-water for blood and a patience that is not human. They no longer want fire at all and will drown one wherever they find it. Attacks: barbed fish-spears, weighted nets, bile, things that rise from the mud under the boardwalk. Death: they sag and pour — the body slumps into black water and peat before it ashes, leaving a slick.
families.roles_lack: healer and reviver — their regeneration is saved for the Mire Mother's fight — and any fast flanker: everything in the mire comes slowly and from below.

families.concept: A fungus that learned to glow the colour of lantern-light, because warm bodies walk toward lamps.
families.lore: In the fog of the mire there is a lamp ahead of you. There is always a lamp ahead of you. 偽燈菌 is the only light in 瑟蘭 that is not fire — a fungus whose fruiting bodies glow the exact amber of a lantern and hang at the height a person would carry one. It grows in warm bodies. The infected do not fall: they lift the "lamp" that has grown from their arm and walk out into the fog to stand where travellers will see them. It is patient, immobile where it can be, and fights by making the ground itself poisonous. Attacks: spore bursts, lobbed pods, clouds that weaken; almost no direct blows. Death: the glow goes out first — instantly, like a pinched wick — and then the body deflates in a puff of spores and ash.
families.roles_lack: support and anything fast — an area-denial family: the fight is about where you are still allowed to stand.

families.concept: The things whose breathing gives the Weeping Mire its name — leeches that drink warmth instead of blood.
families.lore: The mire weeps: a thin rising whine out in the fog, like a child a long way off. It is breathing. 泣蛭 have a row of gill-flutes down each flank and they whistle as they taste the air for heat. They do not drink blood; a victim is found whole and cold, the warmth drawn out through a ring of small round marks. They live in the mud under the boardwalks and come up beneath whatever is warmest. Attacks: latching bites that chill and slow, miasma spat from a reared-up frill, ambush from below. Death: they knot themselves into a ball and deflate; the ash is wet and clumps.
families.roles_lack: every humanoid role, caster and support — a pure serpentine ambush family that is always mixed with Mireborn or False-lamp.

families.concept: The dead of the Brass Dynasty, buried standing to await a sun of their own making, and woken by the storm instead.
families.lore: The Brass Dynasty did not accept the dusk. They would build a sun: 黃銅日輪, a disc of polished brass a mile wide, to catch the light of the stars and the lightning of the storms and pour it down on the city. They spent the kingdom on it. It never lit. Their dead were buried upright in the sand, wound in linen and ringed in brass, facing the disc, to walk again on the first morning — and the storm-lightning that crawls over the ruins now gives them a cruel imitation of it. The Sandbound fight for a dawn that already failed: blade-dancers, disc-throwers, mirror-guards, the mask-makers who keep them presentable and the brass sentinels that guard them all. Attacks: fast curved blades (bleed), returning discs, reflected projectiles, called lightning. Death: the linen empties — sand pours out of the wrappings, the brass rings ring on the floor, and a violet spark earths itself.
families.roles_lack: swarmer and exploder — the dynasty's dead are disciplined and few; the numbers in the sands come from brass-hermits and sand-skinned husks.

families.concept: Desert crawlers that eat verdigris and live inside the dynasty's hollow brass — helmets, gears and storm-jars that scuttle.
families.lore: Brass does not rot, so the dunes are full of it: helmets, masks, cog-wheels, jars. Something moved in. 寄銅蟲 are soft-bodied crawlers that graze on verdigris and wear whatever hollow brass fits them, trading up as they grow the way a shore-crab trades shells. A helmet that walks. A gear that rolls at you. A storm-jar that has learned to spit its lightning. They conduct every strike of the storm and are livelier for it. Attacks: pinches, a corroding sting that strips armour (vulnerable), rolling charges, arc discharges. Death: the brass drops with a clang and rolls away; a small pale thing shrivels out of it and ashes. The shell stays as a prop.
families.roles_lack: caster and support — vermin again, but armoured: the puzzle is the shell, which blocks from the front and from above.

families.concept: The machinery of the Brass Sun, still tracking a light that is not there — until someone brings one.
families.lore: The Brass Sun needed keepers that did not tire: mirror-frames that turned with the stars, carriers that walked the disc's segments up the scaffolds, little winders that kept every spring tight. They are still at it. The engines have no malice and no interest in the living; they have a single instruction — find light, focus it — and for a thousand years there has been none. A hero carrying ember is the brightest thing they have ever tracked. Attacks: focused beams with long telegraphs, mirror-flash stuns, the crushing tread of the carrier. Death: the springs let go — they fold up with a long unwinding rattle, shed plates, and the storm-jar inside bursts in a violet flash. They leave brass scrap, not ash.
families.roles_lack: melee troops, swarmers and casters — an emplacement family that never appears alone; it turns a Sandbound or brass-hermit fight into a positioning problem.

families.concept: The candle-makers of the cathedral city, sealed in their own wax by the Order and stood in the naves as unlit candles.
families.lore: The holy city held the dusk off with ten thousand candles, and its people were chandlers. When the Order took it the chandlers were not killed. They were sealed: their own wax poured over mouth and eyes — the vow of quiet, administered — a wick set in the crown of the head, and each one stood in a nave or a street as a candle that must never be lit. Some have stood so long that they have run together. They hold very still until something warm comes close. And the wick is real: fire lights them, and a lit one burns fast, bright and with no thought but reaching you. Attacks: smothering blows, wax that hardens on you (slow, then root), burning runners. Death: unlit ones crack and slump; lit ones burn down to a pool in seconds — the only family whose death leaves a ground hazard by default.
families.roles_lack: ranged and swarmer — they were made to stand still; the Order's own troops provide the reach and the speed.

families.concept: The cathedral's bells with their tongues cut out — and the ringers the Order hung in their place.
families.lore: A bell is the loudest thing a city owns, so the Order began with the bells: clappers unhooked and carried off, mouths stuffed with wet shroud. That was not quiet enough. The ringers were locked inside — some under the small bells, to walk the streets as warnings; some hung by the feet in the great ones, in place of the tongue. A bell rung with a body does not toll. It makes the opposite of a sound: a ring of dead air that rolls outward and puts things out. Attacks: blind charges, the weight of iron, pulses of silence that weaken and stun. Death: the bell falls and — once, finally — rings. One clear note; allies near it flinch.
families.roles_lack: ranged, swarmer and healer — three heavy, slow pieces built around stun and weaken, intended as the anvil for the Order's hammer.

families.concept: Sparks of the Sun-Forge that refused to go out, fell into the abyss and learned to be afraid of the cold.
families.lore: When the Forge died, not all of its fire died with it. The sparks that would not go out fell into the abyss and lay in the slag for centuries, and fire that is afraid of going out becomes something with a will. 燼魔 are not invaders from another place: they are the Forge's own orphans — clinker and basalt crusted round a core of old fire, feeding themselves anything that burns so that they never have to go dark. They hate the Silence more than they hate the hero, which is why a binder can strike a pact with them. Attacks: claws, hurled cinders, slams, dive-bombing, furnace-mouthed charges. Death: the crust cracks open, the fire inside gets out, and for a second it is beautiful; then slag and ash.
families.roles_lack: support, healer and shield roles — a fiend feeds itself first; nothing in the family protects anything else.

families.concept: The Sun-Forge's inner work-crew, fused to their tools, still working the shift that never ended.
families.lore: The giants carried fuel to the Forge; the 爐僕 worked inside it. Over generations in that heat the crews were rebuilt for the job — bellows for lungs, tongs for hands, a hammer where an arm had been — until it was hard to say where worker ended and tool began. The Forge has been cold a thousand years and nobody has rung the end of the shift. They pump air into dead hearths, pour slag that is not there, strike anvils with nothing on them, and when something warm walks in they finally have material to work. Every attack is tool-work: grip, blast, pour, strike. Death: the tool-parts lock, the body inside gives out, and the thrall stands dead on its feet for a moment before it topples; black iron remains, and ash sifts from the joints.
families.roles_lack: caster, support and healer — labour, not sorcery; they are mixed with fiends, who supply the fire they fan.

families.concept: Pieces of Osaros's sleep that leak out of the abyss — white, soundless outlines where a creature should be.
families.lore: The Lord of Silence sleeps under the dead Forge, and his sleep is not empty. It leaks. 淵寂 are not born and are barely alive: they are holes in the world's noise and warmth that have taken on outlines — pale, smooth, featureless, pierced through. They make no sound at all; near them the hero's own footsteps and fire go quiet (the audio mix ducks, flames shrink). They do not hate. They are what the Order prays to become. They take — heat, sound, the hero's resource; they pull projectiles out of the air; burning ground dies where they pass. Death: no ash. They close, like an eye, to a white line and then to nothing; a moment later the sound comes back in a rush.
families.roles_lack: ranged physical, support and summoner — the Hush adds nothing to the world; every member only subtracts. It is deliberately spread over five rigs so that the endgame's signature family is the most varied in body.

types.silhouette: Upright articulated skeleton, narrow and vertical, with light showing through the ribcage; dented kettle cap, a single pauldron and a notched rusty sword held low. The read is "thin soldier under a round hat brim". Materials: old bone, rust, grave linen; accent: faint pale-blue eye sockets.

Light skeleton under a torn madder-red hood and shawl; a quiver of javelins fans up over the left shoulder like a broken wing and one javelin is cocked in the right hand. Hooded head plus a fan of spikes is the read. Accent: dull red cloth, no glow.

types.anims: Zombie_Scratch, Punch_Jab; idle Zombie_Idle_Loop, run Sprint_Loop
types.silhouette: A child-sized skeleton wrongly assembled from leftovers: one arm far too long and dragging, the other a stump with a rib lashed on as a spike, the skull too big and tilted, no helmet. It scuttles bent double so the long arm trails behind — a lopsided little hook shape. Bone bound with grave cord; no accent.

Broad skeleton hidden from the front behind a coffin lid carried as a tower shield (tapered hexagon, iron cross-straps, bent nails along the rim), a short grave-digger's mattock in the other hand. From any angle the read is "a coffin plank with legs". Materials: rotten oak, iron straps; no accent.

types.anims: Spell_Simple_Shoot (pours ash to revive), Interact; idle Idle_Lantern_Loop
types.silhouette: Stooped skeleton in a long funeral stole hugging a large round-bellied urn against its chest with both arms, the lid tied to its wrist by a cord; ash runs in a thin stream from a crack. Silhouette: a hunched figure with a big sphere where the chest should be. Materials: glazed black clay, grey linen; accent: pale green glow in the urn mouth.

Two skeletons' worth of bone stacked into one wide body: a doubled ribcage like a barrel, a second pair of small arms folded on the chest, and three skulls set in a row across the shoulders with the middle one largest. It swings a headstone lashed to a timber post. Materials: mixed bone, moss-stained granite, rope; accent: three pairs of pale green eye-lights.
Emaciated grey figure with a hunched neck, hanging jaw, sunken ribbed torso and long claws reaching forward: a forward-leaning question mark in rags. Materials: ashen skin, rags; no accent.

types.anims: Zombie_Scratch (burst wind-up); Zombie idle and walk
types.silhouette: Grotesquely swollen: a huge taut belly wider than the shoulders, split skin, stubby fat arms held away from the body — a near-sphere on short legs. Accent: sickly yellow-green pustules that brighten before it bursts.

A husk still wearing the iron collar and waist-chain its family locked on; the chain ends in the torn-out tether post, a heavy stake with a ring, which it drags behind and throws like a flail. Silhouette: a hunched body with a long sagging line running back to a block on the ground. Materials: rust iron, splintered post; no accent.

types.anims: Sword_Attack (double-arm slam), Melee_Hook; Zombie idle and walk
types.silhouette: Four or five husks who froze together sharing warmth and never let go: one walks, the rest are fused to its back and shoulders, so the mass has extra heads at odd heights and a fringe of limp arms that sway. A wide, lumpy, top-heavy mound with no clear neck, under one shared blanket frozen stiff. Accent: a faint orange warmth deep in the middle, visible between the bodies. On death three husks peel off.

A thin husk standing unusually straight, head thrown back, jaw dislocated wide open, both hands cupped at the mouth; a dead lantern hangs from a cord round its neck and swings at the belly. A vertical "trumpet" pose, unmistakable against the stooped pack. No glow — its cue is the sound and a visible plume of breath.

Hooded ash-grey robe with a rope belt, blank oval mask, candle wax crusted on the shoulders, curved dagger held reversed. A plain pointed-hood triangle — the baseline Order silhouette. Accent: cold white mask.

Dark robes with a pale stole, a tall cowl bent forward like a snuffed wick, and a staff topped by a ring of extinguished candles. Tall hooked hood plus ringed staff. Accent: cold white sigil on the chest.

Black corroded full plate, torn cape, a horned and crested helm with one horn snapped off, greatsword. Heavy inverted-triangle torso with an asymmetric horn. Accent: smouldering ember seams in the armour.

Floating bell-shaped vestment thinning into trailing cloth, a tall arched veil over a high comb framing a blindfolded stitched face, hands pressed round a small brass bell, a halo ring standing behind the head. Arch plus ring plus bell-skirt. Accent: cold white halo.

Robed figure with the hood thrown back to show a shaved, wax-sealed scalp, carrying a three-metre pole that ends in a large bell-shaped snuffer cone; a coil of wet shroud is slung like a bandolier across the chest. The pole with its cone stands a head and a half above every other cultist. Materials: blackened brass, grey wool; accent: a thread of white smoke leaking from the cone.

Short hooded cape cut off at the elbows, the hood's long tail hanging to the knees and weighted with a lead seal, the lower face covered by a riveted iron gag-plate; he carries a heavy hand-crossbow whose bow-stave is wider than his own shoulders, braced level on the forearm, and a fan of bolts in a chest bandolier. A wide horizontal bar across a small body, with a long tail behind. Materials: iron, waxed wood; accent: white fletching on the bolt.

types.anims: Spell_Simple_Idle_Loop (heal channel), Melee_Hook (censer swing); idle Idle_Lantern_Loop
types.silhouette: Wide-sleeved deacon's robe under a tall mitre split into two prongs like a tuning fork, with a veil hanging between them, swinging a censer the size of a head on a long chain; a second censer hangs at the hip. A forked hat plus a pendulum arc. Materials: tarnished silver, white linen; accent: pale blue-white smoke that pours downward from the censer.

Bare-chested penitent whose skin is mottled with round burn scars where torches were put out on it; shaved head bound in a rope crown, a snuffed torch stub in each fist. A lean, bare-armed runner with a spiky rope halo — the only unrobed Order silhouette. No glow; soot-black hands.

Wrapped close in wet black shroud strips from crown to ankle, no robe skirt, forearms bare; two long snuffer-hooks (sickle blades with a cone pommel) held out wide and low. A slim, crouched X-shape with two crescents. No accent while stealthed; a white line across the eyes once revealed.

Legless spectral torso whose shredded winding-sheet trails back into wisps, gaunt dark arms with long pale claws, a hollow cowl with two slanted soul-lights, a rusted chain cinched twice round the waist under the Order's seal. Accent: pale blue-white eyes.

No cowl: a long veil of hair and shroud hangs straight down over a bowed head, and two arms far too long reach forward and down, the fingers trailing on the floor. The body is a narrow column bent at the top like a shepherd's crook; a broken chain swings loose from one wrist. Accent: a dim blue glow inside the chest where the heart was.

A dead iron lantern floating at chest height with nobody holding it, its door hanging open and a small face-like wisp pressed against the cracked glass from inside; a short length of carrying-chain dangles underneath. Reads as a small box with a ring handle and a tail. Materials: rusted iron, soot-black glass; accent: cold blue-white wisp inside.

types.anims: Punch_Jab, Punch_Cross, Sword_Regular_A; Roll to dodge
types.silhouette: Small, quick raider in a short patched coat, face smeared white with ash, carrying a pair of oversized wick-shears taken apart — one long blade in each hand. A string of thumb-sized dead lanterns crosses the chest. Compact silhouette with two long narrow triangles at the hands. Materials: leather, ash paint, blued iron; no accent.

Lanky raider in a long coat with the collar turned up and a wide-brimmed lamplighter's hat, carrying a lamplighter's pole twice his height that ends in a hook-and-snuffer head; a coil of rope on one shoulder. Hat brim plus a very long thin diagonal pole with a hooked tip. No accent.

types.status: burn 0.3 over 3 s; burning ground 4 s
types.silhouette: Stocky raider with a yoke-frame on the back carrying six round clay oil pots in two rows, like a rack of skulls behind the shoulders; a lit slow-match is wound round one forearm and a pot is held ready in the throwing hand. Leather hood with a glass eye-slit. Accent: a small warm-orange match glow at the wrist.

Hunched carrier in a soot-blackened apron holding the gang's prize out at arm's length on a short pole: an iron cage the size of a birdcage with a live stolen ember inside. The other arm is wrapped to the shoulder in a thick quilted glove. Silhouette: a bent figure with a barred lantern-box out in front. Accent: the brightest warm amber light any regular enemy carries — it lights its allies.

Huge-bellied raider stripped to the waist, wearing a beacon's iron brazier bowl upside-down as helmet and pauldrons in one piece (the rim rests on his shoulders, an eye-slot hacked in), swinging a maul made from a beacon door-ring on a timber. The dome-on-shoulders head makes him neckless. Materials: soot-black iron, scarred skin, rope; no accent.

Lean handler in a shaggy cloak of cinder-hound pelts with the head-skin pulled up as a hood, a bone whistle on a cord, a short hooked goad, and three slack leashes trailing from the left fist. A shaggy outline with ragged ear-points on the hood. No accent. Arrives with two cinder-hounds.

Lean, deep-chested hound with no eyes — a smooth brow over two flared heat-pit nostrils — upright bat-like ears and a ragged mane of ash-clotted fur along neck and spine, whip tail. A narrow greyhound line with a spiky ridge. Materials: pale hairless flank, ash mane; accent: dull orange inside the nostril pits.

Low, wedge-shaped boar that roots through ash for buried embers: a huge head a third of its length, lower tusks grown forward and flat like two ploughshares, a hump of clinker-crusted bristle over the shoulders, tiny hindquarters. A doorstop wedge. Accent: faint ember glow in the mouth.

Massive shaggy mountain ox whose coat hangs to the ground in ice-matted ropes so that no legs are visible — a moving haystack — with one wide pair of horns curving down and forward past the jaw. A drift of snow rides its back. No glow; a heavy breath plume.

types.status: bleed 0.3 over 3 s; vulnerable 2 s on pounce
types.silhouette: Long-legged white cat with paws twice too large (snowshoes), a very short body, tufted ears as long as its head and a thick club tail held straight up as a balance. A high-shouldered, stilted outline. Accent: two pale green eye-shines — the only eyes in the family.

Low sprawling monitor lizard, belly on the ground and legs out sideways, with a sail of thin verdigris-green plates along the back (it basks on warm metal) and a throat sack that swells before it spits. Very flat and long with a notched sail. Accent: verdigris-green throat glow.

Ragged oversized crow with a heavy pick-axe beak, a bare scorched head and throat (from eating coals) and wing feathers singed to uneven fingers; it carries a stolen ember in its beak. Broad ragged wings, big wedge beak. Accent: a single hot orange point at the beak.

Bat with ears like two dishes, each larger than its body, a flat leaf-nose and a short stub tail; the wing membranes are torn into scallops along the trailing edge. Two big discs on a small body. No accent.

Bloated horsefly the size of a dog: a translucent abdomen like a hanging lamp-globe that fills and glows as it feeds, a long straight needle proboscis, legs dangling in a bunch. A globe hanging under blurred wings. Accent: yellow-green abdomen that brightens to amber when fed.

types.status: weaken 0.2 while inside; dims the hero's light radius
types.silhouette: A cloud of several hundred pale moths drawn as one actor: a churning ball about three metres across, denser at the core, that streams into a comet shape when it moves. No single body. Accent: the wings catch firelight — the cloud glitters warm near any flame and is ash-grey otherwise.

Frost-bitten corpse in a stiff hide coat and rimed fur mantle, spangen cap with nasal, the whole left shoulder and forearm locked in jagged ice, an icicle beard, and a spear whose head has frozen into a long ice blade. Accent: ice blue.

Lean hunched predator with crescent ice horns sweeping out and forward, a sail of ice needles down the spine, and fingers that end in long flat ice blades. Accent: a cold seam glowing under the spine sail.

types.status: chill 0.3 per tick, freeze 1 s on the 4th tick; knockback
types.silhouette: Garrison signaller with a curved signal horn two metres long frozen to his lips and both hands, so the horn points wherever he faces — a great crescent sweeping up over his head. A tattered guidon pole is strapped upright to his back. Crescent plus pole. Accent: ice-blue frost streaming from the horn's bell.

types.status: chill 0.4; root 1 s on the waking strike
types.anims: Sword_Attack, Shield_OneShot; break-out with LayToIdle timing
types.silhouette: A sentry frozen upright inside a rough pillar of clear ice as tall as a door — until he steps out wearing half of it: a slab still encases his head and one whole side like a sentry-box, a round shield is frozen to the other arm, short axe in hand. Reads as a standing block with one arm. Accent: pale blue light refracting through the ice slab.

types.status: chill 0.5; freeze 1 s at the slam's centre
types.silhouette: The garrison's road-clearer: a giant of a man in a hooded sealskin coat as stiff as a bell, with a wooden snow-plough blade — a V-shaped board taller than a door — strapped to his left arm like a ship's prow, and over the right shoulder a long pick whose head is a frozen boulder. A pair of snowshoes is lashed upright on his back like two paddles. A pointed bell with a prow in front. Materials: hide, grey timber, clear ice; accent: ice blue in the boulder's core.

A dead supply mule still walking its route, head low, under a pack-saddle carrying two big kegs of frozen lamp-oil and a rack of bundled spears pointing up like a comb; icicles hang from belly and jaw. A boxy load with a row of spikes on top. Accent: blue-white glow inside the cracked kegs, brightening before it bursts.

A knee-high candle-flame shape made of faceted blue glass, hovering a hand above the ground and leaning the way it moves; three curled tongues, the middle one tallest. A clean teardrop with a forked tip. Accent: ice blue with a pinpoint of warm orange deep inside.

A man-high frozen flame that has grown a torso: its "robe" is a skirt of glass tongues that flares upward (wider at the top of the skirt than at the bottom), its two arms are single long flame-blades, and instead of a head it has a tall split flame-tongue. An inverted cone balanced on a point — everything flares upward. Accent: ice blue with an orange core in the chest.

A dead beacon's iron brazier — a basket of bars a metre wide — worn as a ribcage by a hulking body of blue ice that grew up through it; the frozen fire erupts from the basket top as a crown of glass tongues where a head would be, and the brazier's three legs stick out of its back. Arms are rough ice columns ending in fused clubs. Accent: ice blue glowing through black iron bars.

Flat crab-like crawler whose shell is a cluster of blue glass flame-shards growing upward like a crown of candles; small body, six needle legs, two flat plough-jaws for scraping frozen flame. A low disc with a spiky crown. Accent: ice-blue shard tips.

Soot-black giant bent under a shoulder-yoke as long as he is tall, each end hung with a chained bundle of logs that swings out as he turns; small head pushed forward below the bar, short bowed legs. A wide "T" like a balance scale. Materials: tarred timber, chain, skin like bark; accent: the Forge brand on his chest, a dull orange ring.

types.status: knockback; stun 0.6 s on a direct hit
types.silhouette: Giant carrying a wicker-and-timber hod on his back that rises a full body-height above his head, stacked with tree trunks like arrows in a quiver; he reaches back over his shoulder for the next one. A tall rectangle towering behind a stooped body. Accent: the brand ring on his chest.

types.status: root while held 2 s, then thrown (knockback)
types.silhouette: Giant with a domed wicker cage strapped to his back like an enormous lobster-pot, things still moving inside it, and one arm wrapped to the shoulder in quilted hide that ends in iron grabbing-tongs as long as a man; the other hand is empty and open. A dome on the back plus one over-long pincer arm. Accent: the brand ring, and a faint warm glow leaking from the cage.

types.status: burn 0.4 over 3 s; burning ground 5 s
types.silhouette: Giant burnt hairless and glassy, in a slag-crusted leather apron to the ankles and a riveted iron face-shield with one square window, carrying a coal shovel with a blade the size of a door heaped with glowing slag. Flat rectangular head, apron bell, long shovel. Accent: lava orange on the shovel load and in the brand ring.

Fat segmented larva as long as a forearm, pale and ridged, with a hard black head-capsule and two short hook jaws; it moves in humping inchworm arcs. A string of beads with a dark bead at the front. No accent; wet sheen.

types.anims: Attack1 mandible snap, Attack2 shell ram
types.silhouette: Dog-sized burying beetle: a domed black wing-case with two dull orange bands, a flat shovel-shaped head-shield wider than its body, clubbed antennae, and a scrap of shroud and a tin grave-marker caught on its back. A half-dome behind a wide flat shovel. Accent: the orange bands (not emissive; they read warm in firelight).

types.anims: Attack1 emerge-bite, Attack2 undermine (pit under the target)
types.silhouette: Longer, flatter beetle with enormous spade forelegs held out front like a mole's hands and almost no visible head; the wing-case is ridged and caked with grave soil, a coffin handle hooked on one leg. A wedge with two big paddles. No accent.

Ox-sized beetle carrying a whole coffin on her back, lashed on with roots and her own hardened secretion, the lid ajar and grubs spilling from the gap; her wing-cases are vestigial flaps under it. A long box on six legs with a small shovel head in front. Accent: sickly pale green glow from inside the coffin.

A sawn-off stump the height of a child walking on four splayed root-toes, flat-topped (axe-cut, with the growth rings showing), with two short broken branches for arms. A flat-headed block — the only enemy with a perfectly horizontal top. Materials: charcoal with white ash edges; accent: a thin orange ember line around the cut rim.

types.status: slow 0.2 for 2 s (lit: burn 0.3 over 3 s)
types.silhouette: Tall thin burnt trunk split up the middle into two legs, one arm a long forked branch that reaches the ground, the other snapped short; the top ends in a jagged lightning-split crown with no head. A leaning, asymmetric upside-down "Y". Accent: ember-orange glow deep in the trunk split.

Massive hollow trunk with one great horizontal bough — the gallows arm — growing out at shoulder height on its right, three frayed nooses and a rusted gibbet cage hanging from it and swinging as it walks; the left side is only a stump. An inverted "L": nothing else in the game is that lopsided. Accent: ember glow inside the hollow, seen through a knot-hole mouth.

types.anims: Attack1 lash, Attack2 coil-grab; Spawn = erupt
types.silhouette: A single thick charred taproot that bursts from the ground and stands two metres tall like a rearing snake, tapering to a splintered tip, with a fringe of fine rootlets down its length that twitch. No head — a swaying hooked whip. It does not travel above ground. Accent: orange ember veins that pulse just before it strikes.

types.anims: Zombie_Scratch, Melee_Hook; LayToIdle when it reforms
types.silhouette: A hollow human figure of grey crust with a ragged hole clean through the chest (the background shows through it) and the top of the head missing like a broken eggshell; arms held slightly out as if balancing, fine ash pouring from the elbows. No glow — only a rim of dull red sparks at the edge of the chest hole.

types.status: weaken 0.25 for 4 s; slow 0.3 inside the ash-fall
types.silhouette: The cast of someone who died begging the sky: it walks on its knees (the shins fused into a trailing skirt of ash), back arched, both arms raised straight up with the hands crumbled away to stumps, face tilted up with an open hollow mouth. A "Y" on a mound. Accent: grey; red sparks in the mouth while it casts.

A drift that stood up: a slope-shouldered mass with no neck whose surface is made of dozens of half-emerged ash-casts — faces, backs and reaching arms pressed outward like a relief — and whose fists are knots of fused bodies. It trails a plume from its back as it walks. A soft mountain shape with a ragged plume. Accent: dull red sparks in the deep creases. Bursts into three ash-casts.

types.anims: Attack1 bite, Attack2 ash-blast cone; Spawn = emerge
types.silhouette: A segmented worm as thick as a barrel made of baked ash plates like roof tiles, rising two metres out of the ground; its front end is a flat round sieve-plate full of holes (no jaws) which it tips toward the hero to blow ash. A column with a disc on top. Accent: dull red glow behind the sieve holes.
Spider a hand and a half across with a round pale abdomen wrapped in its own first silk like a tiny bandaged ball, short legs held high. A ball on bent pins. No accent.

Wolf-sized spider with a long narrow abdomen held up and forward over its back like a distaff, spinnerets pointing at the target, and two front legs modified into flat combs that card the silk between them; a half-wound grey shroud trails from the combs. Accent: pale grey-green spinneret tip.

types.status: poison 0.3 over 3 s; slow 0.3 for 2 s
types.silhouette: A small tight body under a cage of very long thin legs that meet the ground in a wide circle, like a hanging candelabrum turned upside down; two fangs as long as daggers point straight down. It descends on a visible thread. Accent: pale green fang tips.

types.anims: Attack1 leg slam, Attack2 lay sac
types.silhouette: Huge spider whose swollen abdomen is plastered with dozens of small silk cocoons — some the size of a hand, some larger — like a nest of bandaged lumps; front legs thick and armoured, a human burial mask stuck over her eye cluster. A great lumpy sphere behind a small masked front. Accent: sickly green glow between the cocoons.

types.anims: Zombie_Scratch, Melee_Hook (stiff swing); Zombie idle and walk
types.silhouette: A human cocoon standing upright: wound so tightly that its arms are bound across the chest and only the forearms have torn free, the head a featureless oval, the feet a single bandaged block that it shuffles. Four taut silk threads rise from shoulders and head into nothing and twitch — it moves like a marionette. A bowling-pin with strings. No accent; grey silk.

A stone knight who has stood up off his own tomb lid and brought half of it with him: a flat rectangular slab is still fused to his back from heels to above the head like a backboard, with a carved pillow behind the helm. Sword held point-down in both hands, feet splayed; from the side he is perfectly flat-backed. Materials: grey limestone (white marble in the Sanctum); accent: sickly green glow in the inscription along the slab edge.

types.anims: Spell_Simple_Shoot (a bow from the waist), Spell_Simple_Idle_Loop
types.silhouette: A robed stone lady whose hands are carved as one block in prayer at the chest and cannot part; she casts by bowing. Tall pointed headdress with a stone veil falling to the hips in stiff vertical pleats, no feet visible — the gown meets the floor as a fluted column. A chess-bishop shape. Accent: green (crypt) or cold white (sanctum) light between the joined palms.

A column-statue that walked out from under its vault: a broad stone figure with both arms raised, carrying a broken length of fluted pillar across its shoulders like a yoke-log, a square capital block still sitting on its head as a hat. Rubble dribbles from the break. A thick "T" with a square on top. No glow except a thin line of green or white at the neck joint.

types.status: bleed 0.3 over 3 s; vulnerable 2 s on the waking strike
types.anims: Sword_Dash (lunge), Sword_Regular_Combo; steps down with LayToIdle timing
types.silhouette: A slender guardian statue that stands in wall niches with a halberd upright in both hands — and still has the niche's pointed stone canopy fused above its head like a tall mitre, plus a fragment of plinth on one foot that makes it limp. A tall spike on top and a long halberd. Accent: eye-slots that light green or white only once it is awake.

types.status: knockback; slow 0.3 for 2 s on the waking pounce
types.anims: Attack1 bite, Attack2 pounce; Spawn = stands up from the lying pose
types.silhouette: The stone hound that was carved lying at the barrow-lord's feet, risen with him: a short-legged, thick-necked dog with a perfectly flat underside (it was part of the lid) and a smooth hollow worn across its back where the lord's heels rested, a carved collar with a ring, ears chipped to stumps. It waits lying down exactly as carved and runs with a stiff rocking-horse gait. A low brick-shaped body with a notch in its back. Accent: green (crypt) or cold white (sanctum) light in the collar ring.

Bent old woman in a cloak of reeds and eel-skins under a wide flat basket-hat dripping moss, with a crooked staff hung with fish-bladders and a toad skull, one hand always raised. A flat disc hat over a hunch. Accent: toxic yellow-green bladders.

types.status: poison 0.3 over 3 s on the slam
types.anims: Sword_Attack, Melee_Hook; Zombie idle and walk
types.silhouette: A mound of peat that grew round a sleeper: no neck, a sloping heap of black mud and roots with a drowned boardwalk plank and a broken eel-trap stuck in its back, arms like wet sacks ending in root-knots; the sleeper's pale face shows low in the chest. A pear shape, heaviest at the bottom. Accent: yellow-green fungus glow on the back.

Lean marsh-man with slick grey-green skin, wearing only a reed kilt and a conical fish-trap as a helmet (a woven funnel that covers the whole head, open point upward); he carries a three-pronged barbed eel-spear taller than himself and a string of dead eels at the belt. Funnel head plus trident. No accent.

Broad, stooped marsh-woman with a huge weighted cast-net draped over one shoulder and trailing behind like a bridal train studded with stone sinkers; a lidded creel basket on her back, cork floats strung round the neck. A wide draped triangle with a dotted hem. No accent.

types.status: slow 0.3 for 2 s; poison 0.2 over 3 s
types.silhouette: A sleeper not finished changing: naked, swollen, peat-black to the chest and corpse-pale above, with a long reed breathing-straw still bound to its mouth and sticking straight up past its head, and a slab of peat stuck to its back like a turtle's shell. The arms hang too long. A round-shouldered drip shape with one thin vertical line above it. No accent.

types.status: pull; poison 0.3 over 3 s; slow 0.3 for 2 s
types.anims: Attack1 tongue lash (line), Attack2 belly slam
types.silhouette: A toad the size of a cart-wheel kept by the marsh-folk for the heat of its fermenting gut: a wide flat body, a translucent belly sack that glows and sloshes, tiny eyes on top, and a woven reed harness with a clay hearth-pot tied on its back. A wide low bun with a lump on top. Accent: yellow-green belly glow.

types.status: poison 0.3 over 3 s; weaken 0.2 inside its cloud
types.anims: Attack1 spore bolt, Attack2 cloud burst
types.silhouette: A fungal stalk exactly the shape of a roadside lantern-post: a leaning pole, a curved hook at the top, and a hanging cap-cluster shaped like a lantern with "panes". Only up close do the gills and the skirt of roots at its base show; it reads as a prop until it moves. Accent: warm lantern amber — deliberately the same colour as real lamps — turning yellow-green when it attacks.

types.anims: Sword_Attack (overhead with the lamp arm), Melee_Hook; idle Idle_Lantern_Loop
types.silhouette: An infected traveller in a rotted travelling cloak with one arm locked straight up and forward as if holding a lantern high — the forearm has become a stalk and the hand a glowing lantern-shaped cap; the other arm hangs dead, sheathed in shelf fungus. The head tilts under a bracket of mushrooms. A figure with one raised arm ending in a lamp. Accent: lantern amber.

types.status: poison ground 5 s; weaken 0.2 for 3 s
types.silhouette: Squat infected whose back and shoulders are covered in a cluster of round puffball pods like a bunch of grapes, which it tears off and throws; where the head was, a tall stack of bracket fungus rises in tiers like a pagoda of plates. A stepped spire over a lumpy back. Accent: yellow-green pods, each with an amber pinpoint.

A flat armoured woodlouse the size of a shield whose plates are overgrown with a row of small upright glowing caps, like a tray of candles on legs; many short legs under a skirt of plates. A low oval with a comb of little lamps. Accent: lantern-amber caps.

Three infected fused back-to-back under a single enormous table-mushroom cap two metres across, its rim hung with a ring of lantern-fruit on threads; six legs but only two thick arms, each twisted together from several limbs. A walking parasol, or a carousel. Accent: a ring of amber lamps under the cap rim, yellow-green gills.

types.status: chill 0.2; slow 0.2 for 2 s; heals itself
types.silhouette: Arm-length flattened leech, as broad as a hand at the middle, with a round sucker-mouth at the front and a visible row of small holes (gill-flutes) along each side; it moves in fast vertical loops. A leaf-shaped ribbon. No glow (the belly flushes dull orange after feeding).

types.status: bleed 0.3 over 3 s; slow 0.3 for 2 s
types.anims: Attack1 lunge-bite, Attack2 tail sweep; Spawn = surface
types.silhouette: Thick-bodied eel with a blunt armoured head like a spade, tiny eyes, a jaw that opens sideways as two plates, and a tattered dorsal fin running the whole back like a row of torn pennants. It surfaces to a third of its length: a rearing column with a ragged crest. No accent.

types.status: poison 0.4 over 4 s; poison ground 4 s
types.silhouette: A slimmer serpent that rears upright and spreads a wide frill of feathery gill-fronds round its neck like a ruff or an opened fan; small head with a tube mouth. A fan on a stalk. Accent: toxic yellow-green frond tips that brighten before it spits.

A leech as thick as a wine-tun rearing three metres, its front end a circular mouth a metre across ringed with small pale feeler-lobes like hands; the flanks are pierced by rows of flute-holes that visibly open and close, and smaller leeches cling along its sides. A fat tapering pillar with a ring on top. Accent: dull orange warmth glowing through the belly skin. Four weepers drop off when it dies.

Whip-thin desiccated blade-dancer wound in sun-bleached linen with streaming strip ends, a coiled head-wrap with two long tails, brass rings stacked on neck, arm and ankles, a curved ringed brass sword. Accent: faint violet eyes in the slit of the head-wrap.

A hollow brass guardian shaped like the tomb-statue of a soldier: a barrel torso of riveted plates with a round glass port in the chest where the storm-jar sits, a smooth domed head with a single vertical slot, tubular limbs with ball joints, and a long-hafted bronze fan-axe. Dome plus barrel, very symmetrical. Accent: violet-white arc light in the chest port and the head slot.

Linen-wound guard with a stack of five razor-edged brass discs carried on the left forearm like bangles the size of plates, one more spinning on the right index finger, and a tall fan-shaped brass back-plate — a small sun-disc on a pole — rising behind the head. A head framed by a semicircle. Accent: violet glint on the disc edges.

types.anims: Shield_Dash, Shield_OneShot, Sword_Regular_A; guard pose Sword_Block
types.silhouette: Heavier guard in a scale skirt and brass face-mask carrying a perfectly round, convex mirror-shield as tall as his torso — a segment of the Brass Sun — and a short stabbing spear. The shield is the brightest polished surface in the region and reflects the hero's own light. A big perfect circle in front of a figure. Accent: the mirror flashes violet-white when it reflects.

Linen-wound priest bent forward under a sealed brass jar strapped upright on his back, taller than his head and crowned with three splayed copper rods like a trident antenna; brass wires run from the jar down both arms to thimbled fingers. A stooped body plus a tall jar with a fork on top. Accent: violet-white sparks crawling on the rods; the jar glows before it discharges.

Squat artisan-priest with a leather apron over his wrappings and a pole strapped upright to his back on which six blank brass face-masks are threaded one above another like beads, rising well over his head and clattering as he walks; a small hammer in one hand and a glowing mask held in tongs in the other. His own face is a mask with no eye-holes. A low figure under a vertical string of ovals. Accent: the violet-hot mask in the tongs.

A dented brass soldier's helmet with a nose-guard and a tattered horsehair crest, running on six thin legs with two small pincers poking out of the face-opening. A helmet shape and nothing else. No glow; a violet glint during storms.

types.anims: Attack1 claw sweep (cone), Attack2 tail sting
types.silhouette: Pony-sized scorpion wearing a brass breastplate over its back as a carapace, its tail threaded through brass rings and tipped with a corroded spearhead three hand-spans long, held high over the body; claws like sugar-tongs. A high question-mark tail over a flat body. Accent: verdigris green on the sting.

types.anims: Attack1 nip, Attack2 tuck (Run clip is the tucked pose; code spins the mesh while it rolls)
types.silhouette: A toothed cog-wheel a metre across standing on edge with a soft many-legged body curled in its hub; it walks awkwardly with the wheel tilted on its back, then tips upright and rolls. A perfect toothed circle. Accent: sparks from the teeth and a violet glow in the hub.

types.status: stun 0.3 s (20% chance); the bolt chains once
types.silhouette: A tall storm-jar lying tilted on eight splayed legs, mouth forward like a cannon, with two copper rods sticking out of the neck as feelers and a tangle of wire dragging behind. A tilted amphora on legs. Accent: violet-white glow in the jar's mouth.

A locust as long as an arm whose forewings are two stiff leaves of beaten brass (it has glued scavenged foil to them), held out flat like a biplane, with saw-edged hind legs trailing. A cross shape with long trailing legs. Accent: brass glint, and violet static along the wing edges in storms.

types.anims: Attack1 focus beam (line), Attack2 flash (cone, stun)
types.silhouette: A tripod of brass legs taller than a man carrying a tilted concave mirror-dish two metres across in a gimbal ring, with a counterweight arm and a small sighting vane; it turns to face the hero with a slow clicking. A dish on a tripod. Accent: the dish gathers a point of white-violet light that grows as it charges.

A towering two-legged brass carrier built like a porter: thick piston legs, a small sunken head-lantern, and on its back an A-frame holding one huge wedge-shaped segment of the Brass Sun, a polished slice that stands above it like a sail or a shark's fin. Its arms are lifting-forks. A fin above a blocky body. Accent: violet-white arcs at the leg joints and in the head-lantern.

A child-sized brass attendant with a round pot body and stick limbs, and instead of a head a large butterfly key that turns constantly; it carries a second, bigger key over its shoulder like a rifle and runs with short quick steps. A pot with a bow-tie head. No glow except a tiny violet pilot-light in the chest.

types.anims: Zombie_Scratch, Sword_Attack (two-hand smother); Zombie idle and walk
types.silhouette: A citizen in a long smock whose whole head and shoulders are hidden under a smooth dome of poured wax with a short wick standing from the crown; thick drips hang from elbows and fingertips like stalactites and trail threads to the ground. The dome is narrower than the shoulders — a candle-end, not a bell — and the arms are free. A round-topped column with fringes. Materials: yellowed tallow over linen; no glow unlit — once lit, a real warm flame on the head.

types.status: burn 0.5 over 4 s; burning wax ground 5 s (slow 0.3)
types.silhouette: A sealed one already alight: the wax dome has half melted away on one side so that a bare jaw shows, the wick is a tall guttering flame that streams backwards as it sprints with arms flung wide, and wax runs off it in ropes. A running figure with a flame plume. Accent: a strong warm candle-flame — it reads as a friendly light until it reaches you.

types.status: slow 0.5 for 3 s; root 1 s on a second hit
types.silhouette: Five or six sealed chandlers who stood too close and ran together: a slumped cone of wax taller than a door with heads, shoulders and praying hands half-sunk in its surface, a dozen dead wicks standing along the top like a row of spines, and two arms that are whole bodies stretched thin. A melted cone with a comb of wicks. No glow; one wick may be burning as decoration.

types.status: slow 0.4 for 3 s; burn 0.2 over 3 s
types.anims: OverhandThrow (ladle of wax), Spell_Simple_Shoot (seals an ally)
types.silhouette: An Order lay-brother in a scorched leather apron and hood carrying a long-handled ladle and, on a chest-harness in front of him, a small iron cauldron of molten wax over a covered coal — the only fire the Order permits. A bundle of blank wicks hangs from his belt like a horse-tail. A pot-bellied silhouette with a long ladle. Accent: a dull warm glow under the cauldron; white wax.

A man with a bronze bell locked down over his head and shoulders to the elbows, so that only forearms and legs show; a padlocked iron strap runs between the legs to hold it on, and a frayed bell-rope trails from the crown behind him. He leans forward and runs blind. A bell on legs — unmistakable. No glow; cold white rim-light on the bell's lip.

A huge ringer in a padded bell-founder's coat, bald, with his ears sealed by wax plugs the size of fists, carrying over one shoulder the iron clapper of a great bell: a tapering shaft as long as he is tall, ending in a ball like a wrecking weight. A coil of bell-rope round the waist. A figure with a giant drumstick. No glow; pale wax plugs.

types.status: weaken 0.3 for 4 s; stun 0.5 s within 3 m
types.silhouette: A great bronze bell floating mouth-down a metre off the ground under a broken stub of its own timber headstock, with a pair of bound legs hanging out of its mouth in place of the clapper, swaying. Chains trail from the headstock. Bell, crossbar on top, legs below. Accent: a cold white ring of light that rolls out from the lip when it "tolls".
Horned demon of charred, cracked rock skin with glowing lava fissures, clawed hands, digitigrade-looking legs and a short barbed tail. Accent: lava orange.

Today this is mon_fiend at 0.6 scale. For its own model (mon_imp): a pot-bellied, big-headed spark-child with stubby legs, horns no more than nubs, oversized hands with one fist always holding a glowing coal, and a tail longer than its body ending in a live ember held up like a wick. A round head plus a long upright tail. Accent: lava-orange coal and tail tip.
Hulking lava troll: enormous shoulders and forearms, a small head sunk between them, slabs of basalt fused to the body, lava cracks, a huge stone maul. Accent: lava orange.

types.status: burn 0.3 over 3 s; burning ground 3 s
types.silhouette: A fiend that is nearly all wing: two broad wings of thin black slag-glass with glowing cracks, a tiny horned body between them, and a long whip tail ending in a heavy cinder that it drops. Wingspan three metres. A wide flat "M" with a weighted tail. Accent: lava-orange cracks, brightest along the leading edges.

A four-legged slab of basalt whose whole front is a mouth: the head is a furnace door that hinges open sideways to show a firebox throat; no eyes, heavy front legs and small hind legs, and a row of chimney-stub vents down the spine that smoke. A doorstop wedge with a row of pipes. Accent: lava orange in the maw and the vents.

A tall, starved fiend whose horns have grown up and together into a closed ring above its head with a flame held in the middle — a living brazier; narrow shoulders, arms to the knees, a skirt of hanging slag plates. It carries nothing. A ring on a stalk. Accent: lava-orange flame in the horn-ring, white-hot while it summons.

types.status: knockback; burn 0.2 over 3 s; doubles burning ground it blows across
types.anims: Spell_Simple_Enter / Spell_Simple_Idle_Loop / Spell_Simple_Exit (pump and blast), Melee_Hook
types.silhouette: A thrall whose chest has been replaced by a great leather concertina bellows wider than his shoulders, its two wooden handles sticking out sideways where arms should start (his real arms work them from below); the nozzle is a long iron pipe rising in front of the face like a trunk. An accordion torso with a forward pipe. Materials: cracked leather, iron hoops; accent: orange glow at the nozzle on the blast.

types.status: root while held 1.2 s; bleed 0.2 over 3 s
types.silhouette: Lean thrall in a riveted iron hood with a single round grille, whose right arm from the elbow is a pair of blacksmith's tongs a metre and a half long, jaws open; the left arm is short and wrapped in chain. Leather apron full of burn holes. A body with one enormous scissor-limb. Accent: jaw tips glowing dull orange.

types.status: burn 0.4 over 3 s; burning ground 5 s
types.silhouette: Thrall walking bent under a crucible carried on his own shoulders in an iron collar-frame — a bucket of molten slag directly above his head, with a pouring lip — and a long-handled dipper in both hands. A scorched hood protects the neck. A bucket-on-head silhouette with a long ladle. Accent: the lava-orange surface of the slag, dripping.

A massive thrall whose right arm and shoulder are an iron drop-hammer assembly: a square block head the size of an anvil on a cranked beam, counterweighted by a ballast drum bolted to the left shoulder; the body lists to one side under it and the left hand only steadies. Lopsided, one side all square iron. Accent: an orange heat-glow on the hammer face after each strike.

A round iron furnace door on a short squat chimney-stump bolted to the floor, with a counterweighted lid that swings up like an eyelid; shut it is a black disc, open it is a white-hot hole. Chains hang from the lid arm. A disc on a stump. Accent: lava orange to white-hot when open, nothing at all when shut.

A hound-shape assembled from chain and clinker: a ribcage of iron hoops with a coal burning inside it, a head that is just a hinged iron jaw-trap, and a length of chain dragging from the collar it was once tethered by. No skin — you can see through it. An open hooped body with a dragging chain. Accent: the orange coal in the chest.

A narrow chalk-white figure with no features, clothing or joints — smooth as a wax model — whose head is a long vertical oval pierced by one clean vertical slot that you can see through; fingers twice human length, held together like blades. Its feet do not quite touch the floor. An exclamation mark with a slit in the dot. Accent: void white with a black slot; no glow — it looks lit by a light that is not there.

A pale figure whose torso is a hoop: from collarbone to hips there is only a wide round hole ringed by a smooth rim, the head sitting on top of the ring and the legs hanging below it; the arms are held out to the sides to keep the ring open. A ring with a head — the level shows through it. Accent: void white; the hole fills with black while it inhales, then flashes white.

types.status: weaken 0.3 for 4 s; slow 0.4 for 3 s
types.silhouette: A wide, sloping pale giant with no head at all — the shoulders rise into a smooth dome — and arms so long that the knuckles drag, each ending in a flat mitten-hand the size of a shield; a single round hole pierces the chest clean through. A hunched arch. Accent: void white; a thin black ring spreads over the ground from its slams.

A thing like a white ribcage with no spine, walking on the tips of its own ribs — six or eight curved prongs meeting the ground — with nothing inside the cage and no head; the "sternum" is a smooth keel on top. An upturned basket on its tines. Accent: void white.

types.status: vulnerable 3 s on pounce; resource drain
types.silhouette: A smooth white quadruped with long front legs and a sloping back, no ears and no tail, and a head that is a blunt wedge with a round hole through it from side to side where the eyes would be. A hyena slope with a perfectly clean outline. Accent: void white; unseen until it pounces, showing only a ripple.

types.status: weaken 0.25 for 3 s; slow 0.3 for 2 s
types.anims: Attack1 strike, Attack2 coil-pulse (ring); Spawn = rise
types.silhouette: A white ribbon-serpent, flat as a strap and as wide as a door plank, that rises from the basalt and stands in a slow corkscrew; no head — the front end simply narrows to a point with a small hole near the tip like the eye of a needle. A spiral ribbon. Accent: void white with a black needle-eye.

A flat white kite shape — a diamond three metres across with no body, flexing gently along its diagonals like a ray in water — with a round hole in the centre and two long ribbon tails. It never flaps. A diamond with a hole. Accent: void white.

reskins.look: Rime-crusted bone, an icicle fringe under the cap brim, the sword sheathed in ice; ice-blue eye-lights.
Hood and shawl stiff with frost; the javelins are icicles.
Joints fused with ice so it runs with a stiff skitter; frost-blue bindings.
The coffin lid is sheathed in a pane of clear ice with a face frozen inside it.
Plate glazed in ice, ember seams replaced by ice-blue seams, a cape frozen mid-flap.

reskins.status: weaken 0.25 for 4 s; chill 0.2; resource drain
reskins.look: Fur-lined grey robe; the snuffer cone is rimed and trails cold fog instead of smoke.
Shroud stiffened into icicles, paler blue soul-lights.
The hair-veil is a curtain of hanging frost; fingertips leave rime on the floor.
Skin green-black and slick, duckweed and leeches on the shoulders.
Belly translucent with marsh gas, a brighter yellow-green.

reskins.status: pull; slow 0.3 for 2 s; poison 0.2 over 3 s
reskins.look: Drags a small boat anchor on a mooring rope instead of a tether post.
A fog-horn of bark is tied over its mouth; mud to the chest. Calls mire husks.
Bog-stained brown bone hung with weed, the sword green with corrosion.
Shawl of rotted net; fishing spears instead of javelins.
The shroud hangs wet and heavy and drips; soul-lights the yellow-green of marsh gas.

reskins.status: slow 0.3 for 2 s; fear 0.8 s (20% chance)
reskins.look: Weed instead of hair; water runs from the sleeves.
Waterlogged black bog-oak with bracket fungus on the cut top. Not flammable.

reskins.status: slow 0.3 for 2 s; poison 0.2 over 3 s
reskins.look: Bog-oak trunk hung with moss curtains; the split glows fungus green. Not flammable.
The bough is hung with eel-traps and drowned nets instead of nooses. Not flammable.
A slick mangrove root with air-roots fringing it. Not flammable.
Sun-dried, leather-brown, wrapped in scraps of bleached linen.

reskins.status: weaken 0.3 for 4 s (bursts into blinding sand)
reskins.look: A dried skin stretched tight over a belly full of sand that hisses from the splits.
Sand-polished bone, a brass cap and a brass sickle-sword.
Bleached shawl; brass-tipped javelins.
Sand-coloured robe, a brass mask, the dagger wired to a small storm-jar at the belt.
Ochre robes; the candle-ring on the staff replaced by copper rods.
Brass snuffer cone that crackles; a dust-veil over the sealed scalp.
Plate heat-blued and glowing at the seams, the cape burnt to a fringe.

regions.note: Act 1, so the mix is simple on purpose: a husk rush, things from below (beetles, roots), and the first human enemies. One giant at most per screen.

dungeons.note: A cellar where a household hid and never came out; Ember-takers now use the upper rooms as a cache, and the beetles have the rest.
Root cave: charwood from the walls, husks and hounds sheltering in it.
Matches the boss's own adds (husks and skeletons).

regions.note: Drilled infantry in the open, elemental attrition near the dead beacons, raiders on the road. The Order is only a small detachment here (snuffers and one knight).

dungeons.note: Garrison hall held by the Order; the prisoners relight the braziers.
Stalker den: rime-horn stalkers, glass-mites and flickers, hearth-bats on the ceiling.
Matches the boss's Frostbound musters.

regions.note: The home of the properly dead. Bone and Order packs are the standard; spiders hold the side halls, effigies the royal barrows, tomb-robbing Ember-takers the entrances.

dungeons.note: Royal barrow: stone and what the stone was guarding.
Bone store: the Unburnt, the spiders that wrap them and the beetles that clean them.
Matches the boss's adds (skeletons, javelineers, acolytes).

regions.note: Everything is slow, poisonous and underneath you. Fast pressure comes only from the mire-skinned husks and the warmth-flies.

dungeons.note: Flooded cellar: leeches in the water, the drowned on the islands.
Hag warren lit only by false lamps.
Matches the boss's brood (mire husks).

regions.note: Act 5: disciplined dead, armoured vermin and machine emplacements. Reflect, returning discs and beams punish standing still and blind fire.

dungeons.note: Workshop: engines, the hermits living in their scrap, sentinels on guard.
Tomb road: the dynasty's dead and the common dead around them.
Matches the boss's adds (revenants, sentinels) plus the Order's envoys.

regions.note: The Order at full strength: every role present. Wax-sealed line the streets as dormant hazards, bells are the heavy pieces, and the first of the Pale Hush leak up through the crypts.

dungeons.note: Abbey: the Order and the citizens it sealed.
Bell-tower vault: bells, marble saints and the old dead beneath them.
Matches the boss's choir and acolytes.

regions.note: Fire against silence: fiends and thralls burn the ground, the Hush puts it out and drains the hero. The most varied body-plan mix in the game (all six rigs appear).

dungeons.note: Forge works: thralls at their posts, fiends in the hearths, a stoker-giant on the floor.
Obsidian rift where the Order meets what it prays to.
The last approach: the Hush, its priests and the fire that still resists them.

rare_elites.where: Roams the dead-forest road at the head of a pack
rare_elites.look: Cinder-hound at twice the size, grey-muzzled, one ear gone, the mane burnt down to a collar of live cinders; a snapped reaver leash still trails from its neck.
mechanics: Pack-father: howls at 75 / 50 / 25% life — every hound within 30 m gains Enrage for 8 s and four fresh hounds run in from off-screen.
If he dies while four or more hounds live, the survivors flee with no loot; kill the pack first for the full drop.

rare_elites.where: Beside the toppled watch-fire north of 斷燈哨站
rare_elites.look: Coldcaller in a keeper's oilskin coat with the outpost's hand-bell rusted into his fist and a lamplighter's hook still strapped to his back.
mechanics: Still calling the alarm: his wail is a 12 m ring (fear 1.5 s) and every wail pulls three husks out of the ground inside the ring.
Only a stagger or stun during the 1.2 s inhale (visible breath plume) stops a wail.

rare_elites.look: Ash-weeper with a veil and train of ash that streams behind her; her hands stay clasped at the chest until she casts.
mechanics: Reforms three times instead of once; each pile lasts 3 s and must be struck to stop it.
Every reform leaves an ash-fall zone (8 s, weaken and slow) centred on the pile, so the field fills up if she is allowed to stand.

rare_elites.look: Gallows-tree with a bough twice as long carrying seven nooses, and a crown of ember-peckers perched along it that scatter when he is struck.
mechanics: Casts three noose-lines in a fan: a caught hero is hoisted for 2 s taking damage (freed early by dealing 15% of his life).
When ignited he drops his burning gibbet cages as three delayed fire circles.

rare_elites.where: The signal ledge above the switchbacks
rare_elites.look: Hornblower whose horn has grown into a great spiral of ice-sheathed ram's horn; his guidon still shows the garrison colours.
mechanics: His blast cone is 14 m long and builds freeze in two ticks instead of four.
Every blast musters a rank: four Frostbound soldiers rise in a line across the far end of the cone and advance in step.

rare_elites.where: Shadows the hero along the cliff path and strikes during blizzard gusts
rare_elites.look: A larger crevice-cat, pure white with black ear-tips; in play usually only its breath plume and eye-shine are visible.
mechanics: Never fully visible: re-stealths 1.5 s after every pounce and leaves three decoy snow-ripples as it does.
The pounce marks its target (bleed and vulnerable 4 s). Any area damage or burning ground reveals it for 3 s.

rare_elites.where: Walks the supply road from end to end, forever
rare_elites.look: Pack-mule loaded three kegs high under a garrison banner, dragging the frozen muleteer who still holds its halter.
mechanics: Does not burst on its first charge: every charge drops one keg that detonates after 2.5 s (frost circle, freeze 1.5 s), up to six on the field.
On death the whole load goes: a 9 m burst with a 3 s telegraph.

rare_elites.where: The dead beacon at the summit
rare_elites.look: A cold-flame spirit grown tall and straight like a great candle, with "wax" runs of ice down its sides and six frozen flickers circling it.
mechanics: Six flickers orbit it as a shield: each absorbs one hit and re-freezes after 10 s.
